task.prompt:
The following 18 bodies are brought into thermal contact inside a thermally insulated container of negligible heat capacity, at a pressure of 1 atm (water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C):
1. glass: mass 210 g, initial temperature 42 °C, specific heat 840 J/(kg·K)
2. ice: mass 32 g, initial temperature -10 °C
3. brass: mass 316 g, initial temperature 19 °C, specific heat 380 J/(kg·K)
4. liquid water: mass 153 g, initial temperature 63 °C
5. liquid water: mass 367 g, initial temperature 12 °C
6. copper: mass 409 g, initial temperature 99 °C, specific heat 385 J/(kg·K)
7. water vapour (steam): mass 12 g, initial temperature 138 °C
8. brass: mass 578 g, initial temperature 53 °C, specific heat 380 J/(kg·K)
9. liquid water: mass 60 g, initial temperature 73 °C
10. lead: mass 827 g, initial temperature -14 °C, specific heat 129 J/(kg·K)
11. granite: mass 679 g, initial temperature 101 °C, specific heat 790 J/(kg·K)
12. water vapour (steam): mass 36 g, initial temperature 118 °C
13. glass: mass 922 g, initial temperature 138 °C, specific heat 840 J/(kg·K)
14. liquid water: mass 250 g, initial temperature 23 °C
15. copper: mass 801 g, initial temperature 113 °C, specific heat 385 J/(kg·K)
16. water vapour (steam): mass 30 g, initial temperature 110 °C
17. zinc: mass 574 g, initial temperature 13 °C, specific heat 388 J/(kg·K)
18. iron: mass 233 g, initial temperature 223 °C, specific heat 449 J/(kg·K)

Constants: specific heat of liquid water 4186 J/(kg·K), of ice 2100 J/(kg·K), of steam 2010 J/(kg·K); latent heat of fusion of ice 3.34·10^5 J/kg; latent heat of vaporisation of water 2.26·10^6 J/kg. The other bodies are solids that do not change phase; their specific heats are given. It is guaranteed that in the final equilibrium all the ice has melted and all the steam has condensed, and the final temperature is strictly between 0 °C and 100 °C.

Find the final equilibrium temperature in °C with 4 significant figures.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
